source2_quote: Joe’s Apartment – 152 Riverside Drive, Between 87th and 88th Streets
creator: Nora Ephron
address_as_given: 152 Riverside Drive (the address on the building's awning)
notes: The film puts 152 Riverside Drive on Joe's awning to explain his screen name, NY152, but no building has that number; location guides place it between West 87th and 88th Streets, between the real 140 and 160 Riverside Drive. The building filmed is 210 Riverside Drive at West 93rd Street, a separate exterior record. Joe moves out to his boat after he and Patricia split.
source_quote: Ignore the ‘152 Riverside Drive’ address – that’s simply to justify Joe’s online name

source2_quote: After Joe decides to leave Patricia, he moves onto his boat which is parked on the Hudson at 79th Street.
creator: Nora Ephron
address_as_given: his boat at the 79th Street Boat Basin, on the Hudson
notes: After he breaks up with Patricia, Joe moves onto the family's boat, moored at the city-run 79th Street Boat Basin at the foot of West 79th Street. The marina is shown on screen and was filmed there; it is not named in dialogue, so the placement is the location guides' identification. The mark covers the marina, not a slip.
source_quote: he moves out to live on the water at the 79th Street Boat Basin, 79th Street at the Hudson River

source2_quote: Kathleen lives in the kind of dreamy, shabby-chic Upper West Side pad that befits the heroine of a Nora Ephron movie
creator: Nora Ephron
notes: The film gives Kathleen no street address; she and Joe are neighbors on the Upper West Side who cross paths at the same Starbucks, Zabar's and Verdi Square. The brownstone shown is 328 West 89th Street, a separate exterior record.
source_quote: As two Upper West Side dwellers, Kathleen and Joe often crossed paths, even before they knew each other.

source2_quote: She leaves him and takes their daughter to New York, where she moves in with her father.
household: with her father and her daughter
creator: Mike Nichols
address_as_given: her father's apartment, the Apthorp, 2211 Broadway
notes: When Rachel leaves Mark in Washington she takes their daughter to New York and moves in with her father; the film shot his building at the Apthorp, the block-square 1908 apartment house on Broadway between West 78th and 79th Streets, where Nora Ephron herself once lived. The film does not name the building in the story. Ephron wrote the screenplay from her 1983 novel, which gives no address for the father's place.
source_quote: In the 1986 dramedy Heartburn, Rachel Samstat (Meryl Streep) heads to the home of her father at The Apthorp after finding out that her husband is cheating on her.
